lesson.title: Wrong examples, wrong answers
lesson.subtitle: How AI learns from labels, and how to keep them right

video.title: Wrong examples, wrong answers
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Last week I played a joke on my little nephew. I showed him a lemon and said “banana”. The next day, he called every lemon a banana! Could a computer be fooled like that too?

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how AI learns from examples, and what happens when some of them are wrong.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Lots of pictures; Each has a label; Finds what's alike; Sorts new fruit.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: To teach a computer to sort fruit, we show it lots of pictures. Each one has a label: “mango” or “lemon”. The computer finds what each kind has in common. Then it sorts new fruit by itself.

scenes.visual: A list: Right labels: it learns well; Wrong labels: it learns mistakes; It can't tell they're wrong.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Those labels are its teacher. If the labels are right, it learns well. But if some labels are wrong, it learns wrong things too. It can't tell that a label is a mistake.

scenes.visual: A list: By accident; Or on purpose, to spoil it; Called “poisoning” the data.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Mistakes can happen by accident. But someone could also add wrong examples on purpose, to spoil the AI. Grown-ups call this “poisoning” the data.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Someone sneaks ten wrong labels into the fruit pictures. What happens when the computer learns from them?

scenes.visual: One big value, 3 → 7: Mistakes in every 100 fruit.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: It makes more mistakes. It learned from every label, the wrong ones too. Now some lemons get sorted as mangoes.

scenes.visual: Cards: Look closely; Odd one out; A big, sweet “lemon”; Probably wrong.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: How can we find the wrong examples? Look for the odd ones out. A “lemon” that is big and very sweet sits right among the mangoes. That label is probably wrong!

scenes.visual: A list: Where are they from?; Look for odd ones out; Fix or remove them.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: People who build AI check where their examples came from. They look for odd ones out. Then they fix them or take them away.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Add wrong labels; Train; Score drops; Find the odd ones.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, slide up the wrong labels and press Train. Watch the line move and the score drop. Then press “Find the odd ones out” to catch them!

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Your class is teaching a computer to sort leaves. A friend labels a few leaves wrongly, as a joke. What should you do?

scenes.visual: The summary: It learns from labels; Wrong labels, wrong answers; Look for odd ones out. Takeaway: Good examples make good AI.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Labels · Wrong answers · Odd ones out
scenes.narration: Fix them, and tell your teacher. Remember: AI learns from examples with labels. Wrong labels teach it wrong answers. And looking for odd ones out helps us find them.

scenes.visual: A list: A friend is the computer; Cards with labels; One wrong label; What did it learn?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: play “Teach the sorter”. One friend is the computer, and learns from picture cards with labels. Sneak in one wrong label, and see what the “computer” learns!

checkpoints.prompt: Someone sneaks wrong labels into the fruit pictures. What happens when the computer learns from them?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right! It learns from every label, the wrong ones too.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. It can't tell a label is wrong, so it learns the mistakes.

checkpoints.prompt: Your class is teaching a computer to sort leaves. A friend labels a few wrongly, as a joke. What should you do?

options.text: Nothing: it's only a few leaves
Fix the labels and tell your teacher
Add more wrong labels for fun

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes! Right labels make a good AI. Fix them, and tell your teacher.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. Even a few wrong labels teach mistakes. Fix them and tell your teacher.
